findings: 2026-11-05: drafted for Mathematics 11 Unit 12 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: In the first line of the solution of Example 15 the book prints the exponent as -ky: \lim_{t \to \infty} A_{0}e^{-ky}. There is no y in the problem; the exponent must be -kt, as in the given function A(t) = A_{0}e^{-kt} and in the book's next line. The answer 0 is correct.

Book correction: The statement of Example 17 prints D(p) = \frac{100}{p+t}, but the solution uses D(p) = \frac{100}{p+1}; t is not defined in the problem. The intended function is D(p) = \frac{100}{p+1}. (The limit is 0 in either case, since t would only be a constant.)
